subject: Request: temporary SLA tier adjustment & credit cap
messages:
From: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@stratos.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@stratos.ai
Date: 2025-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLA tier adjustment & credit cap

Hi Mateo / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StratosAI is excited about the integration potential. Our procurement team ran the numbers and asked whether Redwood can offer a short-term concession to the availability SLA for the first 90 days post-launch. The ask is two-fold:

- Reduce the availability commitment from 99.95% to 99.90% for months 1–3 while traffic and cache warm-up occur.
- Cap monthly service credits to 10% of the monthly invoice for those months.

We understand this is non-standard. The reason: our initial production profile will see heavier asynchronous batch workloads and we want a predictable cap on financial exposure while we validate steady-state behaviors.

Also, can you confirm P95 latency SKUs remain at the agreed 200ms threshold or if any temporary adjustment is required during the ramp?

I attached a short amendment draft (stratos_sla_amendment_draft.pdf) with language the legal team proposed. If Redwood is open, we can run a quick redline pass and try to close this by COB Monday so procurement can finalize payment terms.

Appreciate you both — happy to hop on a 20 min call if more efficient.

Best,
Ryan Cole
Head of Procurement, StratosAI
ryan.cole@stratos.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Notes: referenced amendment attached.
From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@stratos.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-09T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA tier adjustment & credit cap

Ryan — thanks for the clear ask and the draft amendment. Appreciate the upfront rationale.

High level response: we can consider a time-bound availability concession for the ramp window, but a few critical guardrails we'd want in the amendment:

1) A defined start and end date for the temporary tier (e.g., first 90 calendar days following production cutover).
2) A telemetry clause that requires Stratos to share request/ingestion volume for the ramp period or allow Redwood to sample traffic to validate the warm-up claim.
3) A slightly higher credit cap than proposed if availability drops below 99.75% — to keep incentives aligned.
4) Clarify that latency SLO (P95) remains measured on the hosted endpoint and that transient backend maintenance windows are carved out from calculations if notified per the maintenance window clause.

Proposed trade: Redwood accepts 99.90% as the temporary floor for months 1–3 with a hard credit cap at 12% of monthly invoice, provided Stratos agrees to the telemetry clause and a formal cutover date. If availability falls below 99.75% in any month, the cap increases to 20% for that month.

I attached our draft redline (redwood_provisioned_amendment_v1.docx) with inline changes.

If that sounds reasonable, laura and ben — can you review the credit ladder language and confirm we can operationalize the telemetry request?

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@stratos.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA tier adjustment & credit cap

Looping in procurement/finance perspective. Quick operational notes:

- Telemetry: we can accept a one-way telemetry sharing clause. Preferred approach: Stratos exports a daily CSV of request counts, error rates, and average token rates for the ramp window to a shared S3/GCS location. Our SRE will use that to validate any credit triggers.
- Credit ladder: Mateo's 12% / 20% escalation is workable but we prefer a graded ladder for clarity:
  * 99.90%–99.75% => 12% credit cap
  * 99.75%–99.50% => 18% credit cap
  * <99.50% => 25% credit cap
This avoids cliff effects.
- Latency: we will keep P95 at 200ms. If Stratos' bulk batching causes measurable P95 degradation for live endpoints, we'll treat that separately and not as an availability breach unless errors increase.
- Audit window: include a 30-day post-ramp audit right so either side can request a root cause packet for any month with credits.

Ben — can you confirm these numbers are acceptable to finance and if the audit language is standard?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@stratos.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, contracts@stratos.ai
Date: 2025-10-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA tier adjustment & credit cap

Thanks all for the quick turn. This is largely aligned with our internal risk appetite. A few quick replies:

- We can provide the daily telemetry export to a shared S3 bucket; procurement will set the IAM role.
- The graded ladder is cleaner — we accept the 12% / 18% / 25% bands as written.
- We confirm P95 will remain at 200ms for live endpoints; bulk batch paths will be flagged and excluded from availability counts as long as they use distinct input routes (we'll document these).
- Cutover: we'll propose 2025-11-01 as the production cutover date (tentative). The temporary tier would cover 2025-11-01 through 2026-01-31 inclusive.

Assuming Redwood sends a final redline with the graded bands and telemetry clause, we'll instruct legal to sign the amendment. Happy to sign off on email if that speeds things up.

Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to launch.

Regards,
Ryan Cole
Head of Procurement, StratosAI
